# pangolin_resource_mtls_certificate (Resource)

Manages one trusted CA certificate for client-certificate (mTLS) authentication on a resource or a resource policy (Pangolin 1.25.3 or later, enterprise license). Clients must then present a certificate signed by one of the CA certificates. Set exactly one of `resource_id` and `resource_policy_id`.

Pangolin enforces mTLS only when it is enabled **and** at least one CA certificate exists, and refuses to enable it before. That is why the switch is `enable_mtls` here and not an attribute of the resource: a resource that enabled mTLS itself would need its own certificate to exist first, a dependency cycle. Set `enable_mtls = true` on one certificate; it is applied after the certificate is stored. mTLS needs `ssl = true` on an HTTP resource (the server refuses it on tcp / udp resources, and a shared policy that enables mTLS takes precedence over the resource's own setting).

Pangolin has no update route and never returns the PEM: changing `certificate` or `name` replaces the certificate, and the certificate is compared by its SHA-256 `fingerprint`. A PEM bundle is refused: use one resource per CA certificate (at most 20 per resource or policy).

Removing the last CA certificate makes Pangolin switch mTLS off. Import with `resource/{resource_id}/{id}` or `policy/{resource_policy_id}/{id}`; set `certificate` as usual afterwards (it must match the imported fingerprint).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Clients must present a certificate signed by this CA to reach the resource.
# enable_mtls turns the check on after the certificate is stored.
resource "pangolin_resource_mtls_certificate" "ca" {
  resource_id = pangolin_resource.app.id
  name        = "internal CA"
  certificate = file("${path.module}/ca.pem")
  enable_mtls = true
}

# The same on a shared resource policy.
resource "pangolin_resource_mtls_certificate" "policy_ca" {
  resource_policy_id = pangolin_resource_policy.shared.id
  certificate        = file("${path.module}/ca.pem")
  enable_mtls        = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `certificate` (String) The CA certificate, one PEM block. Changing it replaces the certificate.

### Optional

- `enable_mtls` (Boolean) Turn mTLS on for the resource or policy once this certificate is stored. Defaults to `false`, which leaves the setting alone (it does not turn mTLS off, other certificates may have enabled it). Set it on one certificate only. Destroying the certificate does not turn mTLS off unless it is the last one.
- `name` (String) A label for the certificate. Changing it replaces the certificate.
- `resource_id` (Number) The resource trusting the CA. Without a shared policy the certificate goes to the resource's inline policy. Changing it replaces the certificate.
- `resource_policy_id` (Number) The resource policy trusting the CA. Changing it replaces the certificate.

### Read-Only

- `fingerprint` (String) The SHA-256 fingerprint, as computed by Pangolin.
- `id` (Number) The certificate ID.
- `issuer` (String) The certificate issuer.
- `subject` (String) The certificate subject.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a CA certificate as resource/{resource_id}/{id} or policy/{resource_policy_id}/{id}.
# Pangolin never returns the PEM: set `certificate` in the configuration afterwards.
terraform import pangolin_resource_mtls_certificate.ca resource/<resource_id>/<certificate_id>
```
